accepted.question_text: Do there exist overcomplete Gabor frames for L^2(R), meaning systems of the form {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} with g in L^2(R) and parameters a,b>0 that form a frame but not a Riesz basis, together with some ordering {f_k}_{k in I} of the frame elements, such that the ordered frame can be written as {f_k}_{k in I} = {T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded linear operator T and some vector phi?
accepted.context_brief: bounded operator representation of overcomplete Gabor frames

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Does there exist overcomplete Gabor frames {EmbTnag}m,n∈Z and an appropriate ordering on the form {fk}k∈I , such that the operator T in (2.3) is bounded?

accepted.question_text: Assume an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} admits an ordering {f_k} for which {f_k}_{k in I} = {T^k phi}_{k in I} with bounded T. Must such a bounded-operator representation exist for both indexing choices I=N_0={0,1,2,...} and I=Z, or can the existence of a bounded representation depend on whether the ordered orbit is one-sided or two-sided?
accepted.context_brief: indexing dependence for Gabor orbit representations

evidence.quote: (P1-a) Is a representation of the form (2.3) with T bounded available for both indexings I = N0 and I = Z?
For Gabor systems it is not known whether the chosen indexing play a role.

accepted.question_text: Given an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}, which orderings {f_k}_{k in I} of its elements have the property that the ordered frame can be represented as an operator orbit {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for some bounded linear operator T? In other words, can one characterize exactly which permutations or sequential arrangements of the same Gabor frame yield a bounded generating operator?
accepted.context_brief: characterizing admissible orderings of Gabor frames

evidence.quote: (P1-b) Can we characterize the orderings {fk}k∈I of {EmbTnag}m,n∈Z for which a representation as in (2.3) is available with a bounded operator T?

accepted.question_text: Which overcomplete Gabor frames {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} admit at least one ordering {f_k}_{k in I} for which there exists a bounded linear operator T and a vector phi with {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I}? Equivalently, what conditions on the lattice parameters a,b>0 and the window g in L^2(R) determine whether some ordering of the frame can be generated by iterating a bounded operator?
accepted.context_brief: which Gabor frames admit some bounded ordering

evidence.quote: (P1-c) Can we characterize the Gabor frames {EmbTnag}m,n∈Z for which an appropriate ordering on the form {fk}k∈I leads to a bounded operator T in (2.3), i.e., what are the conditions on a, b > 0 and g ∈ L2(R) for this to be possible?

accepted.question_text: Is there a single universal ordering rule {f_k}_{k in I} that works for every overcomplete Gabor frame that admits some bounded-operator orbit representation, so that whenever a frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} is of a type covered by the previous existence question, arranging its elements according to that one rule always yields {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded operator T?
accepted.context_brief: universal ordering for bounded Gabor representations

evidence.quote: (P1-d) Is there a universal ordering on the form {fk}k∈I that applies for all the Gabor frames in (P1-c)?

accepted.question_text: Let phi in L^2(R) and b>0 be such that the translate system {T_{kb} phi}_{k in Z} is an overcomplete frame. Although this system always has the two-sided representation {(T_b)^k phi}_{k in Z} with bounded translation operator T_b, is it possible to reorder the same frame into a one-sided sequence {f_k}_{k=0}^infty and find a bounded linear operator T such that {f_k}_{k=0}^infty={T^k phi}_{k=0}^infty?
accepted.context_brief: one-sided bounded representation for translate frames

evidence.quote: Problem 2: Is it possible to order an overcomplete frame of translates {Tkbϕ}k∈Z on the form {fk}∞k=0 = {Tkϕ}∞k=0 for a bounded operator T?

Using Proposition 2.3 (v) we immediately see that such a system always has the representation {(Tb)kϕ}k∈Z, with the translation operator Tb being bounded. Thus Problem 1 trivially has a positive answer for the index set I = Z. However, it is unclear whether the same is true for the index set I = N0.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a separable Hilbert space H with an overcomplete frame {f_k}_{k=0}^infty whose vectors are uniformly bounded away from zero in norm and for which there is a bounded linear operator T from H to H such that f_k=T^k f_0 for every k>=0? Equivalently, can an overcomplete frame that does not decay in norm still be generated as a one-sided bounded operator orbit?
accepted.context_brief: norm-bounded-below overcomplete operator orbits in Hilbert space

evidence.quote: Problem 3: Let H denote a separable Hilbert space. Do there exist overcomplete frames for H that are norm-bounded below and have a representation {fk}∞k=0 = {Tkf0}∞k=0 for a bounded operator T : H → H?
Intuitively, Lemma 4.1 says that a frame having the desired type of representation must have “infinite excess in all directions.”
